sims.title: Braess's Paradox
sims.caption: Toggle the shortcut road and watch how individually rational routing makes everyone worse off.

sims.title: Structural Cascade
sims.caption: Step through adoption one round at a time — adjust the threshold and see how cluster density can block the cascade.

sims.title: BFS: Distance Layer by Layer
sims.caption: Click any node to start BFS from it. Watch layers expand outward — the layer number IS the distance.

sims.title: Connected Components
sims.caption: Click an edge to remove it; click "Add random edge" to reconnect. Each color is one maximal connected component.

sims.title: Giant Component Emergence
sims.caption: Add edges one by one and watch one component grow to dominate. The largest is the "giant component."

sims.title: Triadic Closure
sims.caption: A and C are both friends with B. Click "Close triangle" to see triadic closure form the A–C edge.

sims.title: Bridges and Local Bridges
sims.caption: Click an edge to remove it. See which removals disconnect the graph (bridge) or just lengthen the path (local bridge).

sims.title: Structural Holes & Brokerage
sims.caption: Compare two nodes: A is deeply embedded in one dense cluster; B spans structural holes between three separate groups.

sims.title: Schelling's Segregation Model
sims.caption: Drag the threshold slider and press Run — watch mild individual preference cascade into neighbourhood-scale segregation.

sims.title: Affiliation Networks and Foci
sims.caption: Click a focus to highlight everyone who shares it — that shared context is the seed of focal closure.

sims.concept: Signed graphs and the balance conditions
sims.title: Signed Triangle Explorer
sims.caption: Click any edge to flip it + / −. The triangle is balanced when it has 1 or 3 positive edges.

sims.title: Balance Theorem: Two Camps
sims.caption: A balanced complete graph MUST split into two friend-cliques at war with each other. Move nodes between camps and watch every triangle stay balanced.
